# Obsidian vault reorganization

## Goal
Reorganize the repository's durable `docs/` and `agents/` markdown knowledge into an Obsidian-friendly vault structure without changing the meaning of the project records.

## Scope
- Inspect current `docs/`, `agents/`, and root note layout.
- Create or update an Obsidian vault entry point and navigation indexes.
- Keep existing project path semantics intact unless a move is clearly safe.
- Avoid moving executable/runtime agent assets.

## Intended changes
1. Infer the smallest vault structure that makes the existing notes usable in Obsidian.
2. Add vault metadata/configuration only where it does not affect code paths.
3. Add indexes/maps that connect project docs, agent workflow material, and remarks.
4. Verify markdown links and repository status after the reorganization.

## Completion notes
- Chose the repository root as the Obsidian vault so existing `docs/`, `agents/`, and `remark/` paths remain stable.
- Added `.obsidian/` configuration that focuses Obsidian on durable markdown knowledge and hides code/build-heavy directories from the file explorer.
- Added `Home.md`, `docs/README.md`, and `remark/README.md`; updated `agents/README.md` and the root `README.md`.

## Verification log
- Verified all new navigation targets exist with the `find` tool.
- Re-read the new/changed navigation files after edits.
- Shell-based scripted link checking could not run because shell execution was cancelled by the environment; no shell output is claimed.

# Tonic DSA knowledge vault

Open this repository root as the Obsidian vault. The vault keeps the existing project paths intact so code, plans, reports, and agent guidance continue to use their repository-native locations.

## Start here

- [[docs/README|Project docs map]] — research plans, reports, specs, and related work.
- [[agents/README|Agent operating materials]] — agent-facing plans, workflow reports, and coding requirements.
- [[remark/README|Research remarks]] — single-point insights distilled from experiments and reviews.
- [[docs/research_plan|Research plan]] — thesis-level narrative for the batching regime change.

## Vault rules

- Keep domain research and validation under `docs/`.
- Keep agent operating material under `agents/`.
- Keep short durable observations under `remark/`.
- Prefer normal relative markdown links for files that may be read outside Obsidian; use wiki links in navigation pages only.

# Project docs map

This directory is the human-facing research knowledge base for the project. It is part of the root Obsidian vault; open [[Home]] first if you want the top-level map.

## Primary entry points

- [[docs/research_plan|Research plan]] — thesis-level narrative and current research positioning.
- [[docs/design_document|Design document]] — system design record for the DSA/stdexec work.
- [[docs/specs/README|Specs]] — local DSA/IAX hardware specs and spec-reading guidance.
- [[docs/related_work/01_host_intra_host_datapath|Related work: host/intra-host datapath]]
- [[docs/related_work/02_batching_submission_regime|Related work: batching/submission regime]]
- [[docs/related_work/03_async_framework_completion_overhead|Related work: async framework completion overhead]]
- [[docs/related_work/04_rpc_acceleration_transports|Related work: RPC acceleration transports]]
- [[docs/related_work/05_intel_accelerators_data_movement_offload|Related work: Intel accelerators and data movement]]
- [[docs/related_work/06_zero_copy_serialization_compression|Related work: zero-copy serialization and compression]]

## Records by purpose

- `plan/YYYY-MM-DD/NN.topic.state.md` — human-readable project plans and completion records.
- `report/benchmarking/` — benchmark findings, plots, and measurement notes.
- `report/architecture/` — architecture decisions and integration history.
- `report/hw_eval/` — hardware evaluation findings.
- `report/literature/` — literature synthesis and paper folders.
- `report/research/` — broader research synthesis.
- `report/integration-review/` — integration risk and review notes.
- `report/api/` — API-facing reports.

## Boundary

Agent execution plans and workflow reports live in [[agents/README|agents/]]. Single-point insights live in [[remark/README|remark/]].

displayContent.text:
# Agent operating materials

This directory holds repository-local material whose primary audience is coding agents rather than the project research narrative.

## Layout

- `CODING_REQUIREMENTS.md` — persistent coding requirements distilled from GSD milestone decisions; read before writing or modifying project code.
- `plan/` — agent execution plans for changes whose primary purpose is agent operation, delegation, tooling, prompt templates, or live-thread workflow.
- `report/workflow/` — durable reports about agent orchestration, task shaping, retrieval strategy, and live-thread workflow.

## Obsidian navigation

- [[Home|Vault home]]
- [[agents/CODING_REQUIREMENTS|Coding requirements]]
- `plan/` — chronological execution plans.
- `report/workflow/` — durable workflow reports.

## Boundary

Keep project research, hardware findings, architecture reports, benchmark results, literature notes, specifications, and human project plans under `docs/`. Put material here when it exists to guide agent operation or preserve agent-workflow design decisions. Agent execution plans still need to be readable project records, not private scratchpads.

Historical plan records may still mention the former docs workflow-report paths; prefer the paths under `agents/` for active references.
